Take {G} off {WHEN}, put {GP} back on {WHEN2}. || Warm in the middle, cold at both ends. Today is a microwave burrito.

{G} can come off {WHEN}, and you won't need {GP} again today. || The weather peaked and didn't crash. Rare, for anything that peaks.
The heat eases {WHEN}, but it stays warm. || From brutal to just rude.
{WHEN} it gets a little less hot. Still warm, though. || Cooler, by frying pan standards.
It cools off a little {WHEN}, but stays warm. || The heat goes down a notch. It has a lot of notches.
The heat eases {WHEN}, but it stays warm. || The heat doesn't break. It just sprains a little.
Take the umbrella for now. The rain stops {WHENSTOP}. || Some weather app said 'all day.' I'm not naming names.
Take the umbrella for now. The rain stops later. || It stops. That's already more than most wedding speeches manage.
The rain stops later, but you'll want the umbrella for now. || Somebody's bad knee saw this coming too. I have better sources.
The snow stops {WHENSTOP}. || The bread and milk panic can stand down.
The snow stops later. || The 'when I was a kid' stories won't, though.
It stops snowing {WHENSTOP}. || Then every snow blower on the block starts up at once. Very peaceful.
The snow pauses later and starts again {WHENP}. || The snowplow drivers get a coffee break. Exactly one.
Snow for now, then a break, then more snow {WHENP}. || The break is just the sky reloading.
Snow for now, then a break, then more snow {WHENP}. || The break is long enough for everyone to post photos. Then the photos are out of date.
Snow for now, then a break, then more snow {WHENP}. || Even the weather repeats itself. At least I wait a day.
There's a shower passing through {WHENP}, so bring the umbrella. || Just enough rain to make every car need a wash.
There's a short rain shower {WHENP}. Have the umbrella with you. || Short enough for people to argue about whether it counted.
Bring the umbrella. There's a shower {WHENP}. || I've seen longer commercials.
Bring the umbrella. There's a shower {WHENP}. || Small talk from the sky. Brief, damp, pointless.
Nothing changes for the rest of the night. || Even the weather keeps better hours than most people.
Nothing changes for the rest of the night. || Even the raccoons find this forecast boring. They're out anyway.
Nothing changes for the rest of the night. || My favorite kind of overtime.
What you have on is fine for the rest of the night. || Same as before, only darker. Groundbreaking work, if I say so myself.
The sweater can come off {WHEN}. || Every chair back in town is about to wear a sweater.
{WHEN} it's warm enough for short sleeves, so the sweater can come off. || Short sleeves. Bold claim from the weather. I'll allow it.
It warms up {WHEN}, so the sweater can come off. || The temperature goes up. Morale goes up slightly less.

{WHEN} it's going to be really hot, so have water with you. || Shade becomes a group activity.

Today everyone's a forecaster. Their whole forecast is 'cold.'
Fun fact: I have no ears. Today that's a flex.
Local screen still doesn't own a coat. Sources say it's thriving.
The evening's forecast took me four seconds. I spent the rest admiring it.
The weather has nothing left to say today. I, on the other hand, could go on.
Of all the screens you'll look at tonight, I'm the only one with nothing to sell.
I was into shade before it was popular.
Dogs lie flat on cool tiles in this heat. I've been flat my whole life.
Steering wheels are untouchable today. I'm untouchable every day.
Freezing rain looks harmless from in here. That's the trouble with in here.
The sidewalks may be glazed like a donut. All of the slip, none of the sugar.
The fastest way anywhere today is slowly.
This forecast holds till morning. Most promises made at this hour don't.
My night mode is the same as my day mode. Effortless.
Late-night thoughts are rarely accurate. Mine always are.
Lights are going off all over the neighborhood. Mine never came on.
Bedtime story: once upon a time, the weather stayed exactly the same. The end.
Off for a bit, back on later. The hokey pokey, with outerwear.
The weather's doing that thing where it's nice, then remembers who it is.
At least the weather's mood swings come with a schedule.
Peak warmth comes and goes. Peak me lasts all day.
Being right later costs one layer now. Bargain.
Today's understudy: {GP}. The big scene is later.
Now: fine. Later: less fine. Me: fine throughout.
Today's weather is a bait and switch. I don't do bait.
I wouldn't suggest a coat on a morning like this for fun. I don't have fun.
Long pants: the most boring good decision of the day.
A party up front, business later. The day's a reverse mullet.
Rain doesn't bother me. I don't do hair.
The corner store's umbrella prices just went up. My forecast's still free.
Some people call this cozy weather. Those people are indoors.
I never drink water and I'm fine. Please don't take me as a role model.
Heatstroke is not a souvenir. Leave it outside.
The shade is the VIP section today. Getting in is free.
The morning will say no. The day will say yes. I side with the day.
Not shorts weather yet. Shorts weather soon. I deal in soon.
Every cold morning has one person in shorts. Today that's the right person.
Fortune favors the bare-kneed.
I love a snow forecast. It's the one time everyone listens.
Snow muffles everything. Even the people complaining about it.
Snow sticks to everything except plans.
Outfit settled for the whole day. Most decisions never get that far.
Zero changes all day. Easiest money I never made.
Today's forecast fits on a sticky note. With room for a doodle.
Lightning goes for tall things. I'm small, flat and indoors. Feeling great.
Counting between flash and bang: the only math everyone does for fun.
Hair, umbrella, dignity: a storm takes them in that order.
Dear thunder, we heard you the first time.
Dog walks will be brisk today. The dogs don't get a vote.
A forecast this easy, even a phone could get it right.
Other weather apps would show a shivering emoji. I have standards.
Everyone out there is breathing little clouds. Amateurs. I draw mine.
The pigeons are puffed up to twice their size. I only do that when complimented.
Bundled up, you almost look mysterious. Don't talk, it ruins it.
You'll hold a hot drink like it loves you back.
The cold is a great excuse to cancel plans. Shame you'd need plans first.
The cold makes everyone's eyes water. You'll finally look moved by something.
Later, the people who brought a layer get very smug. I know the feeling.
The day gets a little worse later. I'm reporting it, not endorsing it.
The later drawing takes more ink. The things I do for accuracy.
Strong start, weak finish. Today has New Year's resolution energy.
Later the weather has a 'we need to talk' moment.
Later you'll say you're 'not a cold-weather person.' You're not much of a warm-weather one either.
One more layer later, and you'll still find a way to look underdressed.
Later you'll want a layer and a hug. One of those is easy to find.
The weather has one good idea in the middle, then drops it.
The day starts and ends in the same layer. In between, it gets ideas.
Today's weather goes out, has a nice time, and comes back cold.
The warmth is a free trial today. It cancels itself.
Today the temperature takes the scenic route back to where it started.
The day warms up for a while. Unlike anyone who's met you.
Today your outfit gets more variety than your conversation.
The weather changes its mind twice today. That's twice more than you ever have.
Seat belt buckles everywhere are turning into branding irons.
Days like this, I'm very glad I don't have armpits.
Any chocolate bar outdoors today is a drink.
Your hair will give up in this heat. It's been close for years.
You'll say 'I'm melting' like it's a new joke. It wasn't new the first time.
Today's tips: drink water, find shade, avoid mirrors.
Weather this nice deserves full color. It gets grayscale. I'm doing my best.
The parks will be full of people pretending they do this every weekend.
Today's weather has no notes. I usually have notes.
Weather this nice is terrible for small talk. What's left to complain about?
You'll sit outside for ten minutes and call yourself 'outdoorsy.'
Lovely day. Shame about the company.
Weather like this flatters everyone. It'll do what it can with you.
The drawings barely change. You haven't either, in years.
Today you have no weather to blame. Awkward.
Snow is my easiest drawing. I just leave bits out.
Snow is the only weather people count down to. Nobody counts down to me.
When it snows, people stand at the window like it's TV. I'm right here.
I've had a white background all along. Snow's just catching up.
Every pair of 'water-resistant' shoes is about to be tested.
Snow is just weather with good PR.
You'll get excited like a kid. You'll look like a tired adult.
Snow in the forecast. You'll have something to talk about for once.
Snow: soft, quiet, pretty. You: one out of three on a good day.
Later the weather gets a little nicer. It's a slow learner.
The later drawing has less to draw. I'm not complaining.
The cold leaves early today. Best guest all year.
The cold gives up later. Weak. I can hold one picture for days.
The day improves as it goes on. One of you does.
Later you'll take a layer off and look around like someone should applaud.
Warmer later. The weather will be the most pleasant thing in your life.
Later the cold loses interest in you. Everyone does eventually.
Later you'll carry the layer you took off. Finally, someone sticking around for you.
Rain makes everyone walk faster and nobody arrive sooner.
Someone will look up today and ask 'is that rain?' I already knew.
Half the people out there will carry umbrellas. The other half will carry regret.
Rain is the only thing that makes a bus shelter popular.
A bit of rain and you'll look like you've been through something. More than usual.
The umbrella will be the most organized thing about you today.
You'll do a little jog to dodge the rain. Most athletic you'll look all week.
You'll huddle under an awning with strangers. They'll wish they'd picked another awning.

Later it cools off. I'd sugarcoat it, but I only come in black and white.
Later it cools off. Most people out there dressed for the good part. Optimists.
Now: 'Lovely out.' Later: 'Since when is it this cold?'
It warms up, then cools back down. Lost-and-found bins love days like this.
Warm for a bit, then cool again. At any moment, half the town is dressed wrong.
It warms up, then cools again. Every grandma who said 'take something warm' wins today.
Warm, then cool again. I'd call it unpredictable, but I predicted it.
Cold. No, warm. Actually, cold. The weather's holding up the line.
Perfect weather out there, I'm told. I don't get a window.
Perfect weather. Whatever goes wrong today, the weather has an alibi.
Perfect weather. Good moods everywhere. It's exhausting to watch.
Later it warms up. Turns out the early bird just gets the cold.
Later it warms up. The day gets a redemption arc. I never needed one.
Later it warms up. Every bag in town gets one layer heavier.
Later it warms up. Fashionably late, the weather. I'm never late. I'm never anywhere.
Rain. Somewhere a bus is lining up the big puddle.
Rain. Every ride app just raised its prices. Coincidence, I'm sure.
Rain. Somebody will say 'nice weather for ducks.' The ducks didn't ask.
Wet sidewalks, wet dogs, wet socks. I'm the only dry thing in this sentence.
Cool out. Perfect operating temperature for me. Not that anyone asked.
Cool out. Dogs in little sweaters everywhere. Finally, some competition.
Cool out. The yearly 'is it too early for soup?' debate is open.
